author: WP14
summary: Input chapter (keyboard, mouse, logical coordinates, gamepad, touch, TextInputEXT, CNA::Input extensions, focus, platform limits). Its architecture model (bridge-fed InputManager read by GetState) and many renderer, cursor, sensor and haptic statements are stale even at its own pin: TARGET publishes keyboard/mouse snapshots from platform services, twelve cursor descriptions, a WindowId renderer registry and self-acquiring sensor/haptic subsystems. The site had strong internals (Input internals) but lacked the public contract detail; four new deep dives now carry it.

sections.heading: Logical coordinates are a renderer contract

concepts.text: CNA's Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Input namespace covers Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, TouchPanel and TextInputEXT, with CNA-only extension classes (CNA::Input) layered underneath.

The input module's automated evidence is a large test corpus plus a compile-time freeze of the strict API; the Bible's figure of 522 cases is a different count method from the site's 47 test sources and 523 static definitions.
concepts.note: Bible count 522 replaced by the site canonical 47 sources / 523 definitions.

concepts.text: Automated input evidence does not replace physical keyboard, mouse, gamepad, touchscreen, IME and high-density display verification.

concepts.text: F9 and F10 simulate graphics-context loss and restoration in Game::PollEvents (DebugSimulateContextLoss / DebugRestoreContext on non-repeat presses).
Because each event reaches the input bridge first, F9 and F10 still reach Keyboard::GetState(); applications can observe but cannot suppress the debug action and should not bind gameplay to them.

Public input members fall into tiers: STRICT (frozen XNA/FNA surface), EXT (FNA extensions with the EXT suffix) and CNAEXT (CNA-only additions); CNA's own glossary also names an FNA-compatible behaviour tier.
concepts.note: Adds the FNA-compatible tier and the rule that non-enum EXT members also carry the CNAEXT marker.

concepts.text: PublicApiInputSignatureFreezeTests.cpp compile-checks the frozen member set by taking addresses or static_asserting every member.
Keyboard is static-only; GetState(PlayerIndex) ignores its argument and returns the same state as GetState().
KeyboardState stores pressed keys in a std::unordered_set<Keys> instead of FNA's bitfield while preserving the observable queries.
GetHashCode keeps FNA's formula: the eight 32-bit words are rebuilt from the set and XORed.
Keys has exactly 160 values numerically identical to FNA's (Windows virtual-key codes), pinned value by value by a test.
Odd values such as Pause = 0x13, Kana = 0x15 and ChatPadGreen = 0xCA are preserved exactly rather than renumbered, because bindings persist keys by number.

Claim that MouseCursor wraps SDL_Cursor* with eleven lazily created stock cursors: at TARGET MouseCursor holds a description only, the platform service creates native cursors, and there are twelve stock shapes as lazily constructed function-local statics.
concepts.note: Twelve shapes (including WaitArrow); no SDL_Cursor* in the input module.

Beyond GetState and SetPosition, Mouse exposes relative mode and window/capture-related EXT methods.
IsRelativeMouseModeEXT toggles relative (pointer-lock) mode in which motion is reported as unbounded deltas, the standard technique for FPS camera look.
concepts.note: Implemented by the platform mouse service (IPlatformMouse::SetRelativeMode), not SDL directly.

concepts.text: While relative mode is active motion deltas accumulate separately and GetState drains them; outside relative mode nothing accumulates.
concepts.note: At TARGET the service accumulates SDL relative state; the bridge accumulator is legacy/test-only. The claim that toggling flushes stale deltas was not re-established.

concepts.note: TARGET detail added: on platforms without the GlobalPointer capability (native Wayland, terminal) these calls throw PlatformNotSupportedException uncaught.

GestureSample carries GestureType, Timestamp and up to two positions and deltas; the second pair is used only by two-finger gestures such as Pinch.

TouchPanel::GetCapabilities() enumerates platform touch devices on every call, then falls back to the sticky observed-touch flag or a live touch, so it can report a device before the first interaction.

GestureSample::Timestamp deliberately differs from an FNA defect: FNA computes TimeSpan.FromTicks(Environment.TickCount), treating milliseconds as 100-ns ticks.
CNA converts milliseconds to ticks; neither engine defines an absolute epoch, and a regression test asserts non-negative, strictly increasing timestamps under an advanced test clock.

issues.text: DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12 and FREEDIRECT implement TransformWindowToLogical/TransformLogicalToWindow but never call IGraphicsRenderer::RegisterForWindow, so Mouse, SetPosition and touch pass window coordinates through unchanged under a virtual resolution.

On renderers whose TransformWindowToLogical returns false in a letterbox bar (EasyGL identities, OPENGL4, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, SVG_DOM, HTML_DOM), Mouse::GetState and the bridge report the raw window coordinate instead of an out-of-range logical one.

Mouse::GetGlobalPositionEXT, WarpGlobalEXT and SetCaptureEXT do not catch PlatformNotSupportedException, which the native Wayland and terminal mouse services throw, contradicting Mouse.cpp's comment that a platform without a desktop pointer answers (0, 0).
WebGPU/SDL_GPU high-density error recorded in the Bible is absent at TARGET: both convert between client units and drawable pixels.
Vulkan now registers for a window and maps input coordinates (Bible said no override).
CNA::Input::Sensors never initializing the sensor subsystem (latent no-op).
CNA::Input::Haptics never initializing the haptic subsystem.
F9/F10 unconditionally trigger the renderer's context-loss debug seam in Game::PollEvents in every build; games cannot suppress it.
OemBackslash (the ISO 102nd key), VolumeMute and 38 other Keys have no scancode mapping, so the scancode/name helpers return None or empty for them.
TouchCollection.IsReadOnly is advisory while mutators work: deliberate FNA parity, documented as intentional in TARGET tests (docs/input.html calls it a known contract bug).
WindowFocusLostDoesNotClearHeldKeysMatchingFna checks only the bridge's legacy accumulator; public keyboard snapshot behaviour across focus loss is not tested per platform.
Fifteen manual-hardware input checks remain blocked; joystick, host sensor, power, gamepad-extension and IME behaviour are unverified on real hardware.
Wayland gives clients no desktop pointer coordinates; browsers hide gamepads until a button press and gate pointer lock on a user gesture.
